svg.title: Two paths out of one tools/call, and only one of them loops back
svg.desc: One tools slash call request at the top splits into two zones. The left zone, badged protocol error, covers an unknown method, a missing required metadata field, a tool name the server does not have, and an internal failure. Its response is a JSON-RPC error object with a numeric code and no result member, badged as not always HTTP 200 because minus 32601 is a 404 and minus 32020 is a 400. It ends at the client, which a model may be shown but rarely recovers from. The right zone, badged execution error, covers a value out of range, a failed upstream call, a business rule that said no, and an expired handle. Its response is a successful result, badged HTTP 200 always, carrying isError true and a content block, and it is fed back to the model, which reads the message and calls again with a fix. A dashed arrow leaves that box, runs around the outside of the figure and returns to the original request, so only the right-hand path is a loop and the left-hand one dead-ends. A band at the bottom states the rule that decides which path applies, and records that the pinned Python SDK sends an unknown tool name down the right-hand path regardless of what the specification says.
svg.text: Two paths out of one tools/call
Only one of them carries an error member, and only one of them is always HTTP 200.
Unknown method. Missing required _meta. A tool
name the server does not have. An internal failure.
a model may be shown it, and rarely recovers
A value out of range. An upstream call that failed.
A business rule that said no. An expired handle.
it reads the message and calls again with a fix
The rule: an error from inside the tool belongs in the result, with isError set.
An error in finding the tool, or in the shape of the request, belongs in the JSON-RPC error object.
The pinned Python SDK sends an unknown tool name down the right-hand path anyway. Section 7.
